items.title: store() with SHARING_NONE or SHARING_CONFIG copies the adopted template's un-rebuilt .dht/.dpt files after an O1 rebuild, so the operator's own synced snapshot reloads with the stale root hash
items.component: Emulator core: machine::store (src/machine.cpp ~453-481) with machine::clear_hash_tree / hash_tree::clear
items.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md: 'storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines'); the store sharing modes none/config may be off the production path (machine-API reading)
items.severity: Critical (if a production node stores adopted templates with sharing none/config) / Medium (machine API operation off the honest operator's path)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. The O1 exclusion covers cached data that survives adoption 'without a rebuild'; here the operator rebuilds as O1 requires and the emulator re-emits the pre-rebuild files. Section 5: 'A defect that defeats the rebuild itself, or that damages a directory while O2 guarantees it, is not excused by them.' The reloaded directory was written and synced by the operator's own process and never shared, so O2 guarantees it. 2 Role: storing machines is Honest operator per AUDIT.md. 3 High/Medium: if sharing none/config is off the honest operator's path, Medium: 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9).' 4 Critical: on the path ('Obtaining its valid template ... rebuilding its cached hash-tree data (O1)', 'Storing and reloading the machine') it violates R9 ('every snapshot the emulator itself writes') and R1's clause on cached data written by the operator's own process. Code checked: store copies c.dht_filename/c.dpt_filename as a trusted pair for unshared ranges.
items.reason: Code confirmed: the unshared branch of machine::store copies the source directory's dht/dpt files, which clear_hash_tree never rewrote (private mappings). Hunter reproduced a wrong reload hash for none and config. Critical on the honest path, Medium off it.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: after adopting a foreign stored machine with clear_hash_tree=true (O1), machine::store(dir, SHARING_NONE) or store(dir, SHARING_CONFIG) for ranges with shared=false copies the ORIGINAL backing file and its ORIGINAL .dht/.dpt files (src/machine.cpp machine::store, unshared branch ~460-475: os::copy_file(c.dht_filename, ...), os::copy_file(c.dpt_filename, ...)). clear_hash_tree (src/hash-tree.cpp hash_tree::clear ~744) only clears in-memory trees, which for an unshared load are MAP_PRIVATE, so the files keep the template's stale cached data. After sync_stored, reloading the operator's own directory without clear_hash_tree gives the stale root hash, verify_hash_tree fails, and later hashes stay wrong. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL section 5 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too ... A defect that defeats the rebuild itself ... is not excused by them'; R9 'The content hash must equal the root of the actual contents. This applies to every cached, incremental, or persisted hash ... and every snapshot the emulator itself writes' (a directory O2 guarantees); R1 'On the honest operator's path, it [cached hash-tree data] was either written by the operator's own process into a directory that O2 guarantees, or rebuilt from the contents on adoption (O1). This rule applies to it'. Test idea (hunter): copy bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template/machine, populate its cache (SHARING_ALL load + get_root_hash), patch bytes of a RAM page in the .bin behind the cache's back, load with {clear_hash_tree=true} and record H (must differ from the stale hash); for SHARING_NONE and SHARING_CONFIG: store to a fresh dir, sync_stored, reload without clear_hash_tree, assert get_root_hash()==H and verify_hash_tree()==true. Fails now; SHARING_ALL is the passing control. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFSTORED/scripts/storenone.lua. Reviewer must decide whether store with sharing none/config is on a production node's path (both ratings).

items.title: clone_stored hard-links a template's read-only files and keeps short backing files, so a valid template distributed read-only or trimmed cannot be cloned and loaded with sharing
items.component: Emulator core: machine::clone_stored, os::clone_file (src/os-filesystem.cpp ~577-622), os::mapped_memory shared-write checks; callers PRT stored player (prt.lua ~3209-3216) and CLI clone:
items.role: Honest operator (cloning/loading machines); the PRT player and CLI that fail are Support
items.severity: Medium (support player/CLI stand-in for a completeness failure) / Critical (if clone plus shared load is the honest operator's adoption path: section 8 'nothing it carries outside the hashed state may ... crash the honest operator') / Low (if documented hard-link behavior and the unshared workaround are accepted)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: the template meets every valid-template condition (unshared load with clear_hash_tree gives the commitment), so the exclusion for snapshots that do not meet them does not apply; section 8: 'Once a snapshot meets them, nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory.' Not excused by O1 (the load fails before the rebuild) or O2. 2 Role: clone/load are Honest operator; the visible failures are in the Support player and CLI. 3 High/Medium: no wrong hash; the persistence-failure Medium case needs 'an uncommon host setup that the manual documents', which a read-only template is not. 4 Critical reading: R4 and 'Obtaining its valid template' on the honest operator's path if clone + shared load is how the operator adopts. Deciding facts: whether a loud load exception is a 'crash', and whether a working alternative path (unshared load then store SHARING_ALL) satisfies R4. Same gap as R1-O1-1 (loud load error), different root cause and fix.
items.reason: Template attributes outside the hashed state (mode bits, file length) make clone plus shared load throw; reproduced by the hunter. Readings give Medium to Critical, Low only if the documented hard-link behavior excuses it. Unsure, kept.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: os::clone_file (src/os-filesystem.cpp ~577-622) hard-links any file without write permission bits (else reflink, fallback copy that keeps the mode), and machine::clone_stored (src/machine.cpp ~526-577) clones every data/dht/dpt/sht/phtc file as is, without normalizing length. A shared-write load then refuses read-only or multiply-linked files (src/os-mapped-memory.cpp ~59-69 check_shared_write_backing_file) and backing files shorter than the range (~164-175). So a valid template whose files are read-only (chmod a-w, tar/OCI packaging) or whose RAM .bin has trailing zero pages trimmed (same content hash, loads unshared via backing_gap) cannot be adopted by clone_stored + load(SHARING_ALL, clear_hash_tree), which the PRT stored player (doc/recipes/prt.lua ~3209-3216) and the CLI '--load=<dir>,clone:<src>' do. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL section 8 out-of-scope note: 'Once a snapshot meets them [the valid-template conditions], nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory'; R4 'From any reachable state ... the honest operator can always compute the claim'; honest operator's path includes 'Obtaining its valid template'. Test idea (hunter): copy a harness template; (A) chmod a-w its files, (B) separately truncate its RAM .bin to the last nonzero page; assert the unshared clear_hash_tree load gives the reference hash, then clone_stored and assert load(clone, {clear_hash_tree=true}, SHARING_ALL) succeeds with the same hash (fails now: 'is read-only and cannot be shared for writing' / 'length ... does not match desired backing length'). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFSTORED/scripts/ro.lua and short.lua. Note the manual says 'Read-only backing files are hard-linked' (doc/README.md ~1150), and store(SHARING_ALL) of an unshared load is a workaround; reviewer must weigh both.

items.title: Manual and DTB declare Sv39-only address translation, but every path accepts satp MODE=9 and walks Sv48 page tables
items.component: Interpreter (src/interpret.cpp write_csr_satp, src/riscv-warl.hpp WARL_satp, src/translate-virtual-address.hpp) vs doc/README.md 'The main processor' and src/dtb.cpp mmu-type
items.role: Honest operator (interpreter, AUDIT.md table); the defect may be in the manual
items.severity: Medium (undocumented deterministic deviation consistent across all paths) / Critical (literal R7: address translation is a listed area where 'any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest') / Low (if the manual's 'support the Sv39 mode' is read as non-exhaustive)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion; guest-triggered. 2 Role: interpreter, Honest operator. 3 Medium: 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)'; with the contradiction clause 'It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right' (manual doc/README.md ~7313: 'Cartesi Machines support the Sv39 mode ... organized by a three-level page table'; the manual's flash-drive notes ~7493-7513 argue from Sv48, so the manual is itself inconsistent). 4 Critical only under the literal R7 reading for the address-translation area. Same rating pattern as R1-R7-2 (Zcb).
items.reason: Code and manual checked: manual states Sv39 (three-level), DTB says riscv,sv39, satp accepts Sv48 on all paths (hunter ran native/uarch/EVM). Medium under the section 8 Medium case; readings differ (Critical literal R7, Low non-exhaustive).
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: the manual (doc/README.md ~7311-7318) specifies 'Cartesi Machines support the Sv39 mode of address translation ... organized by a three-level page table' and src/dtb.cpp advertises mmu-type 'riscv,sv39', but write_csr_satp (src/interpret.cpp ~2233-2283) and WARL_satp (src/riscv-warl.hpp) accept satp MODE=9 (Sv48) and translate_virtual_address (src/translate-virtual-address.hpp ~139-150) walks four levels with terapages; only Sv57 is compiled out (src/riscv-constants.hpp NO_SATP_MODE_SV57). satp.MODE is WARL: a write of an unsupported mode must leave satp unchanged. All paths agree (native, uarch, Solidity step), so this is a deviation from the documented architecture, not a divergence. Required behavior: R7 'The emulator implements the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation ... Address translation and memory permissions'; section 8 Medium 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths ...' and 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' Test idea (hunter): bare-metal guest in M-mode writes satp = (9<<60)|ppn, reads satp back and halts with (satp>>60) as exit code; assert the read-back MODE is the previous value (0), as the Sv39-only manual and the WARL rule require; it reads 9 on audit/prt2. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFGUESTSTATE/guest.c, run-native.lua, evm-sample.lua. Reviewer should give Medium / Critical (literal R7) / Low (manual non-exhaustive) as in R1-R7-2.

items.title: Manual's /dev/cmio section says the host returns the request type in the yield's DATA field; the emulator, libcmt and the manual's HTIF section put it in REASON with DATA as the length
items.component: Manual doc/README.md ('The /dev/cmio device', ~7234-7241) vs input delivery (src/send-cmio-response.cpp) and the manual's HTIF section (~7660-7668)
items.role: Specification (the manual) vs input delivery (Honest operator); guest software (libcmt) agrees with the code
items.severity: Critical (literal contradiction clause: if the /dev/cmio sentence were right, every delivery deviates in the yield interface's reason encoding, an R7 area) / Low (the HTIF register-level section is normative and matches the code; documentation defect only)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no excluded trigger. The /dev/cmio ABI is a Linux kernel interface (kernel not in scope), but the sentence describes what 'the host sets' on resume. 2 Role: manual vs input delivery, Honest operator. 3 Medium: the consistent-deviation case does not apply because R7 lists 'the yield interface (contents, lengths, and reason encoding)' as relied on. 4 Critical under section 8: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' 5 Low if the HTIF section (which matches) is taken as the governing statement. Manual text checked: ~7236 says 'the host sets the `data` field on resume to HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE or HTIF_YIELD_REASON_INSPECT_STATE'; ~7666 says 'The REASON field in fromhost carries the request type, and the DATA field carries the request length'.
items.reason: Contradiction confirmed in the manual text. The threat model's contradiction clause read literally gives Critical; reading the matching HTIF section as normative gives Low. Unsure which section governs, kept with both ratings.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/README.md, /dev/cmio section (~7234-7241): for HTIF_YIELD_MANUAL_REASON_RX_ACCEPTED 'the host sets the `data` field on resume to HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE or HTIF_YIELD_REASON_INSPECT_STATE to indicate the type of the freshly loaded input'. The emulator writes fromhost = (request type << 32) | input length, i.e. REASON = request type and DATA = length (src/send-cmio-response.cpp send_cmio_response; regenerated SendCmioResponse.sol; libcmt io.c/rollup.c decode it that way), and the manual's HTIF Yield section (~7664-7668) says 'The REASON field in fromhost carries the request type, and the DATA field carries the request length in bytes'. A guest written against the /dev/cmio section misreads every input (length >= 292 for InputBox inputs read as a request type). Required behavior: R7 'The emulator implements ... the devices as the manual documents them ... The rx buffer, the tx buffer, and the yield interface (contents, lengths, and reason encoding)'; section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' Test idea (hunter): load bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template (or the valid template), deliver an advance input of length L=300, and assert that htif_fromhost satisfies every manual section: REASON==ADVANCE_STATE and DATA==L (HTIF section) and DATA==ADVANCE_STATE (/dev/cmio section); both cannot hold, so the test exits 1 until the manual is corrected (a practical form: assert the /dev/cmio section no longer says the host sets the data field to the request type, plus assert the code's encoding). Evidence: code reading; differential delivery-length experiment /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFINPUT/lengths.lua (all paths agree). Reviewer must decide which manual section governs (Critical literal / Low).

items.title: PRT stored player retains only 32 input boundaries per epoch, so reaching a disputed input replays about 3n/64 inputs of an n-input epoch per match
items.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua STORED_MACHINE_CACHE_CAPACITY = 32, machine_cache_methods:consider, find_nearest_entry, run_to_epoch_input_offset)
items.role: Support (PRT player); stands in for the honest operator
items.severity: Medium (support stand-in for a Critical R12 per-match cost that grows with the input count)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. The trigger is the input count and dispute positions (section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts', 'Steer the dispute to any position'); the outputs/yields exclusion does not cover inputs. 2 Role: Support; 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3 High constant-factor case does not fit (factor grows with n). 4 Critical in the honest-operator role: R12 'Reaching that position costs at most the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary, which the application's per-input usage bounds. A7 must cover that cost a bounded number of times for every match' and 'a bounded cost ... per match'. Capped at Medium. Code checked: capacity 32 with gap doubling (prt.lua ~901, ~1217-1245).
items.reason: Cache policy confirmed in prt.lua: 32 entries with doubling gap, so per-match replay grows linearly with the epoch's inputs, against R12's per-input bound. Support, so Medium.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/recipes/prt.lua keeps at most STORED_MACHINE_CACHE_CAPACITY = 32 machines at input boundaries per epoch (line 901; machine_cache_methods:consider ~1217-1245 doubles input_gap when full). Every per-match operation that needs a machine (collect_mcycle_bundle ~2296, build_uarch_cycle_computation_hash ~2315, collect_uarch_cycle_bundle ~2334, event_handler.prove_state_transition ~1956) goes through new_machine_pair_at_epoch_input_offset (~2055-2060, stored ~3040-3052) -> find_nearest_entry (~1247-1258) -> run_to_epoch_input_offset (~2150-2172), which replays every input between the nearest entry and the disputed input (delivery, run to fixed point, stored-pair commit each). With n inputs the worst replay is about 3n/64 inputs (47 at n=1024, 49,151 at 2^20). The single agreed pair helps only the latest bisection. Required behavior: R12 'Each is measured from a machine at its starting position. Reaching that position costs at most the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary, which the application's per-input usage bounds. A7 must cover that cost a bounded number of times for every match' and 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator ... has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match'. Test idea (hunter): new_stored_player on a copy of baremetal-template in the XFS reflink mount, deliver N=512 empty-payload inputs via stored_event_handler.input_added + idle, seal with epoch_sealed(N); shadow player.run_to_input_mcycle_offset on the instance to count calls; call player:new_machine_pair_at_epoch_input_offset(k) for k just before the second-to-last cache entry (or event_handler.prove_state_transition(player, k, 0, 0)); assert the replayed-input count is at most a constant independent of N (e.g. <= 1). Today about 3N/64 (24 for N=512), doubling with N. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFINPUTCOUNT/cache-gap.lua and replay-cost.lua (0.29 s per replayed input on the Linux template).

items.title: PRT player copies and keccak-hashes the guest-declared tx-buffer payload (up to 2 MiB) at every automatic yield of its claim pass, ~170-470x the emulator's per-yield collection cost
items.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua run_to_stop ~1397-1410, run_to_input_mcycle_offset on_yield_automatic ~2078-2091, run_next_input); CLI run_to_stop shares the pattern
items.role: Support (PRT player, CLI); stands in for the honest operator
items.severity: Medium (support stand-in for a High constant-factor R12 defect) / Out of scope (if the outputs/yields exclusion covers every bounded per-yield cost)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: the exclusion 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields ... as long as ... each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12)' may apply, since the per-yield cost is bounded (2 MiB). Against it: the defect multiplies the cost of each yield by a guest-declared length the guest does not pay for in mcycles (same gap as R1-R8-3). 2 Role: Support; stands in for the honest operator computing claims. 3 High in that role: 'A defect that lets the guest ... multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor ... A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect' (operation: a part of a claim; payloads are 'opaque guest data', section 4). Capped at Medium. Code checked: run_to_stop calls receive_cmio_request on every automatic yield when on_yield_automatic is set, which run_next_input always sets; TX_OUTPUT payloads are keccak-hashed. Distinct from R1-R8-1 (memory of one hash per output; different fix).
items.reason: Code confirmed: the claim pass reads min(DATA, 2 MiB) of the tx buffer at every automatic yield and hashes outputs. Medium as a support stand-in for High; Out of scope only under the broad yield-exclusion reading.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: while computing its mcycle claim, the PRT player (doc/recipes/prt.lua run_next_input -> run_to_input_mcycle_offset ~2065-2124 -> run_to_stop ~1397-1410) calls receive_cmio_request(machine) at every automatic yield, which copies min(htif_tohost_data, 2 MiB) bytes of the tx buffer (src/machine.cpp machine::receive_cmio_request ~1986-2016; over JSON-RPC the Lua binding src/clua-i-machine.cpp ~1300-1335 always requests the 2 MiB worst case), and for TX_OUTPUT keccak-hashes it. DATA is guest-declared: a 2-instruction loop storing tohost = yield|automatic|TX_OUTPUT|0x200000 yields every 2 mcycles without writing the tx buffer. Measured 30 us/yield for collect alone vs 5,225 us/yield with the player's receive+keccak (local), 128 us vs 60,512 us (JSON-RPC). Required behavior (honest-operator role, capped at Medium for support): section 8 High 'A defect that lets the guest ... multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect ... A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect'; R12 lists 'a part of a claim'; section 4 'The outputs Merkle root, the output payloads, and every other yield reason are opaque guest data that the state merely commits to'. Test idea (hunter): bare-metal template guest that accepts, then per advance input runs K=50 tohost stores of yield|automatic|TX_OUTPUT|0x200000 and accepts with the empty outputs root; build a player (prt.new_player or new_stored_player), run run_next_input on one input with the pair machine's receive_cmio_request wrapped to sum #data; assert total bytes read do not depend on DATA (e.g. <= 32 x manual yields). Exits 1 today (50 x 2 MiB). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFYIELD/yield-loop.S, measure.lua, measure2.lua. Reviewer must address the outputs/yields exclusion reading (Out of scope vs Medium).

items.title: PRT stored player refuses every valid template that already commits to outputs: store_first_epoch_checkpoint asserts the tx buffer holds the empty outputs root
items.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua store_first_epoch_checkpoint ~2741-2777; crisium.lua epoch-0 checkpoint flow ~225-260)
items.role: Support (PRT player); stands in for the honest operator
items.severity: Medium (support stand-in for a Critical R4 failure on 'Obtaining its valid template') / Low (if PRT deployments are read as genesis-only, manual ~2392 'A template is the genesis of a Cartesi Rollups application')
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. Section 2's valid template explicitly allows a tx buffer holding 'the outputs Merkle root of every output that the application accepted before it, which at genesis is the root of the empty outputs tree', so non-genesis templates are valid; the manual documents them (~2414 '--assert-rolling-template=outputs_merkle_root:<filename>'). 2 Role: Support. 3 As support: Medium when the stand-in role rates High or Critical. 4 Stand-in: R4 'the honest operator can always compute the claim' on the honest operator's path ('Obtaining its valid template'), Critical. Capped at Medium. Code checked: prt.lua line 2761 asserts 'template machine has an output history'.
items.reason: Assert confirmed at prt.lua:2761 with an always-empty frontier; claims do not depend on outputs, yet the player cannot start on a valid non-genesis template. Medium as support; Low only if PRT is genesis-only.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/recipes/prt.lua store_first_epoch_checkpoint (~2741-2777) builds outputs_frontier = new_outputs_frontier() (always empty, ~2463-2473) and asserts machine:read_memory(CMIO_TX_BUFFER_ADDRESS, WORD_SIZE) == outputs_root, raising 'template machine has an output history' (line 2761). It takes no frontier or last-output proof argument, and crisium.lua (~234-237) requires checkpoints/epoch-0, so the stored player cannot start on any template whose tx buffer commits to earlier outputs. Claims do not depend on outputs. Required behavior: THREAT_MODEL section 2 valid template: 'Its tx buffer holds the outputs Merkle root of every output that the application accepted before it, which at genesis is the root of the empty outputs tree'; R4 'From any reachable state ... the honest operator can always compute the claim'; honest operator's path: 'Obtaining its valid template'; section 8 out-of-scope note: 'If it stopped, any claim could win'. Test idea (hunter): build a bare-metal template guest that emits one tx-output automatic yield, writes the matching outputs root (keccak leaf of the output in a height-63 tree) to the tx buffer and yields rx-accepted; store it; call prt.store_first_epoch_checkpoint(template_dir, prt.new_geometry(11), dir) in pcall; require success (and a stored player able to compute the epoch-0 claim); exit 1 on 'template machine has an output history'. Evidence: code reading only. Reviewer: check whether the manual or Dave restrict PRT to genesis templates (Low reading); DaveConsensus emits EpochSealed(0, ..., bytes32(0) outputs root) for epoch 0.

items.title: PRT player's epoch-0 listener fetches InputAdded only from the consensus deployment block, but DaveConsensus seals into epoch 0 every input the application already had, so the player crash-loops
items.component: PRT player process: doc/recipes/crisium.lua (first_block ~125, first_input_block ~267) with prt-epoch.lua (get_logs ~37, seal assert ~95-98); compared with DaveConsensus constructor
items.role: Support (PRT player); stands in for the honest operator
items.severity: Medium (support stand-in for a Critical R4 input-assignment failure) / Low (if applications created separately from their DaveConsensus are not a supported deployment)
items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: not by trigger (inputs from untrusted senders; DaveConsensus assigns them within A3). 2 Role: Support. 3 No listed High/Medium case in the stand-in role. 4 Stand-in: R4 'It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3)' and section 8 Critical 'A crash, hang ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator must process'. Capped: Medium. 5 Low if the deployment shape (ApplicationFactory app with a later-deployed DaveConsensus) is unsupported. Code checked: crisium.lua:267 'previous_seal and ... or first_block', first_block = getDeploymentBlockNumber; DaveConsensus constructor seals epoch 0 with _nextInputIndexUpperBound(0). Distinct from R1-A3-1 (later epochs, previous-seal branch, backlog past the 2^24 cap): different branch, trigger and fix (fallback must start at the application's or InputBox's first input, not the consensus deployment).
items.reason: Code confirmed: epoch-0 listener starts at the consensus deployment block while DaveConsensus seals all prior inputs into epoch 0. Medium as support if non-factory deployments count; Low otherwise. Variant of R1-A3-1 at another branch.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/recipes/crisium.lua sets first_block = consensus.getDeploymentBlockNumber() (line 125) and for epoch 0 first_input_block = previous_seal and previous_seal.log.blockNumber or first_block (line 267), so prt-epoch.lua poll() (line 37) fetches InputAdded logs only from the consensus deployment block. The DaveConsensus constructor (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol ~141-145) seals epoch 0 with inputIndexUpperBound = _nextInputIndexUpperBound(0) = min(InputBox.getNumberOfInputs(app), 2^24), so inputs added to the application before the consensus existed belong to epoch 0 but are never fetched; prt-epoch's seal assert (~95-98, 'sealed input count mismatch') fires and prt-supervise relaunches into the same failure. Reachable when the application is created with ApplicationFactory.newApplication pointing at the future (CREATE2) DaveConsensus address and inputs arrive before DaveConsensus is deployed; DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp (one transaction) cannot reach it. Related to R1-A3-1 (later epochs, previous-seal branch). Required behavior (stand-in role, capped Medium): R4 'It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3)'; section 8 Critical 'A crash, hang ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator must process'. Test idea (hunter): without a chain, build prt-epoch.new with first_input_block as crisium computes it and a fake log history holding two InputAdded logs in a block before first_block and EpochSealed(0, 0, 2) at first_block; assert poll() delivers both inputs and does not raise. Chain variant: ApplicationFactory app with CREATE2 validator address, add 2 inputs, deploy DaveConsensus later, run crisium.lua --kind=honest; it exits with 'sealed input count mismatch'. Evidence: code reading only. Reviewer must decide whether this deployment shape is supported (Medium) or not (Low).

items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. 2 Role: Referee model; section 3 'rated as if the manual were right' and the manual sides with prt.lua ('any holder of that claim may answer it'), so the defect is Dave's permissiveness. 3 No High/Medium case fits. 4 Critical needs a violated rule or obligation: Dave still checks every move against the claim's own commitment, so extra movers can only defend a claim with correct data; the honest operator holds its claim in both; A1-A8 all still hold, and the adversary can already hold and answer for any claim (section 7). The section 5 sentence 'Any other disagreement ... is a defect' names a defect but no class. 5 Low. Same reading as the dropped R1-A2-2 (joins), at different sites with a different fix, so distinct.
items.reason: No rule or obligation is violated: extra movers in Dave can only act with data matching the claim's commitment and gain nothing beyond section 7 capabilities; Low by the R1-A2-2 reading of section 5. Second opinion should re-check with R1-A2-2.

items.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. 2 Role: Support; Medium only if the stand-in role rates High or Critical. 3 Stand-in: R12 allows it: 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain, keeping and persisting its own records ... has a bounded cost per input ... and its total grows only with the inputs, yields, and matches of the epochs still open.' Retained memory is about 3x each input's bytes and is dropped with the epoch. The High constant-factor case applies to 'an operation listed in R12', and chain observation is not listed. 4 No rule violated. 5 Low.
items.reason: Memory is bounded per input and grows only with open epochs' inputs, which R12 explicitly permits; the constant-factor High case covers only operations listed in R12. Support Low, as the hunter rated it.

threat_model_gaps: Self-contradictory manual: section 8's clause 'It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right' does not say which statement governs when two manual sections contradict each other and the code matches one of them (R2-DFINPUT-1: /dev/cmio section vs HTIF section on REASON/DATA).

Medium case vs R7: the Medium case for 'an undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on' conflicts with R7's statement that in its listed areas 'any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths'; also unclear whether the manual's 'support the Sv39 mode' is exhaustive for optional spec features such as Sv48 (R2-DFGUESTSTATE-1; same pattern as R1-R7-2).

Store sharing modes and O1: unclear whether storing with sharing none/config (documented rollback semantics that copy the initial backing files) is on the honest operator's path, and whether R9's 'every snapshot the emulator itself writes' covers a rollback copy that re-emits the foreign cached hash-tree data an O1 rebuild discarded (R2-DFSTORED-1).

Attributes outside the hashed state: unclear whether file mode bits, link counts and backing-file lengths of a template are things 'it carries outside the hashed state' that may not 'crash the honest operator', and whether R4 is met when one adoption path (unshared load then store) works while the documented clone path fails loudly (R2-DFSTORED-2; related to R1-O1-1).

R12 'nearest retained input boundary': the model does not say how many input boundaries the honest operator must retain; 'which the application's per-input usage bounds' implies one per input, but an operator that retains fewer is not explicitly forbidden (R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1).

Constant-factor High case scope: it covers only 'an operation listed in R12', so constant-factor memory or time overheads in the honest operator's work outside the emulator (chain observation, records) have no class beyond R12's per-input bound (R2-DFCHAIN-1). The outputs/yields exclusion's 'each yield costs it a bounded amount' still leaves open whether a bounded but guest-declared per-yield cost (2 MiB payload copied without the guest writing it) is excused (R2-DFYIELD-1; extends the R1-R8-3 gap).

Supported deployment shapes: the model does not say whether the honest operator must support an application whose input record starts before its consensus contract exists (ApplicationFactory app with a later DaveConsensus), which decides Medium vs Low (R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-2).

Genesis vs non-genesis templates: section 2's valid template allows a tx buffer with prior outputs, while the manual says 'A template is the genesis of a Cartesi Rollups application' and DaveConsensus seals epoch 0 with a zero outputs root; unclear whether PRT deployments must support non-genesis templates (R2-DFOUTPUT-1).

Section 5's 'Any other disagreement between a deployed referee and the model is a defect' still has no class when the disagreement changes no outcome; R2-DFCLAIM-1 extends R1-A2-2 from joins to every match move (who may open, seal, prove a leaf, or claim a timeout win).
